findings.item: (а) checkability, and the rule that a micro-amendment does not weaken
findings.what: The new reader obligation at the end of criterion 2 (lines 16504-16512) is ambiguous and in one place weaker than the sentence it follows. (1) «two rounds» is used as «group 1, then group 2» (round 1: the en pairs of five keys; round 2: the ru->en pair of now_idea_s), so on one reading every pair is read by one reader only and a pair marked in round 1 is rewritten but never read again. In the sentence before it, in decisions/0079 item 7 («2-3 rounds») and in the run that read these keys (docs/uat/REQ-113.md, Translation readers: round 1 and round 2 each read all pairs, with a different reader) a round is a full reading of the pairs by a fresh reader and a rewritten pair goes into the next round. A validator at step 9 cannot tell which reading the requirement means, so it cannot answer yes or no. (2) «no kk round is asked for them here» exempts the kk values of now_idea_s and now_closing from the general sentence of the same criterion («the pairs of the new and the changed keys in kk and in en go to reader agents ... in two rounds») and departs from decision 0126 О10 («the kk values are drafts for the reader rounds; disputed lines go to FOR_NATIVE_SPEAKER»). That sentence is a criterion, so an exception to it is a weakening unless it is stated as a decision of the owner or ORCH with its reason; the step-01 task asked only for the en pairs and the ru->en pair and did not decide the kk readers.
findings.needed_for_pass: State in the criterion, so that only one reading is possible, what a round is (how many fresh readers read which pairs in each round, and that a marked pair is read again in the next round), and say whether the kk values of now_idea_s and now_closing go to the kk readers like the other new kk drafts or are exempt, naming the decision that exempts them. The wording is the author's. ORCH may take the kk question to the owner; then the criterion says what stands until he answers.
